name: tutorial-playthrough
description: Full tutorial playthrough at Tutorial Pit: hiring employees, seismic surveying, drill planning, blasting, contract management, building infrastructure, and completing the campaign introduction

The bump is exactly those four, so every cash figure from the drill wait onward is the pre-#553 schedule unchanged.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #553: the drag rectangle was shrunk from (15,15)-(25,25) to (15,15)-(21,21). Command and click stay equivalent -- the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3) computes cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1, so round(6/3)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for this rectangle, exactly what the command declares. The shrink is the point: drill_hole is now real queued work, and a lone driller with one drill_rig and no living quarters collapses from fatigue partway through a pattern (sandbox-measured: hole 9 of 9 lands at tick 119, hole 16 of 16 not until tick ~400). 16 holes would have made this file a study of one worker's stamina rather than a tutorial playthrough. depth stays 6, the panel default this step never clicks away from. Blast consequences re-measured at the smaller pattern rather than carried over -- see the blast step below. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json/save-load-visual.json/weather-flood.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission kept the drill_rig busy (fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks command mode never should have spent. Confirmed exact: adding the real default here reproduces interaction mode's own $126,884 figure at the very next charge step, and the same fixed $108 offset carries unchanged through every remaining cash checkpoint in this file (the second drill_plan below needs no change -- its own diameter default happens not to move the total further).

expect.note: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 9 holes -- they are ghosts until the driller drives the drill_rig to each one, so holeCount is 0 here and the wait is the step below.

steps.description: #553: the single driller/drill_rig sinks all 16 ordered holes. Sandbox-measured; the pad is what the step below asserts against, not a guess.

Finding #40: the corrected 16-hole grid (vs. the originally-declared 9) is dense and energetic enough to kill both employees standing nearby -- confirmed via direct trace (state.damage.deathCount goes 0->2, both the surveyor and the driller, neither of whom this file ever dispatches away from the blast area first). This is a real, verified consequence of fixing the grid-spacing bug, not a scenario-authoring mistake to route around: the file's own later steps never depend on employee #1 or #2 specifically again (later roles are filled by newly-hired employees #3/#4), so the playthrough continues normally with a smaller, grimmer workforce -- exactly what a real player who dragged this same rectangle would experience.

confirmed via direct trace: safety crashes 50 -> ~20 over these 3 ticks (recentAccidents * 5 per tick against the two deaths from the blast above) -- decreased rather than an exact value since the precise magnitude depends on the accident-recency window's exact tick alignment, which real wall-clock ticking in interaction mode is not guaranteed to reproduce bit-for-bit.

#553: contract ids renumbered 1/2/3 -> 5/10/11. The drill wait above spends 130 ticks, and the available pool refreshes on its own clock (REFRESH_INTERVAL, Contract.ts) -- contracts 1-3 were shifted out of it long before this step is reached. 5, 10 and 11 are what the pool actually holds here, and they are the three whose deadlines (91/87/69 ticks) outlast the second drill wait plus the closing tick, so `campaign status` still counts three active contracts at the end. The `tick 10` closing step is `tick 5` for the same reason: at 10 the 69-tick contract expires one tick before the assertion reads it.

#513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="5"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #5 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled at this point. ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of rubble in storage against a 430 kg contract. Still true post-#552 (self-dispatching hauling): no debris_hauler exists yet at this point in the file (bought only much later, step 23) -- there is nothing for auto-dispatch to claim with yet, manual or otherwise. The console command is no better: it returns success:false ("Not enough stored material: 0.0 kg available") and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so `contract deliver 5 amount:5000` is a silent no-op in BOTH modes today. `expect.blocked` is what now pins it down -- the button must be in the DOM and refused, with `expect.usable` on the panel's own storage link proving the panel is really open, so "blocked" cannot pass just because nothing is on screen.

expect.note: stays active/undelivered -- economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:24,24
steps.description: #553: pattern moved from (8,8)-(12,12) to (24,24)-(28,28). The freight_warehouse built at (6,6) earlier in this file occupies ground the old rectangle reached: two of its four holes were ordered onto cells no driller can stand on, so they stayed ghosts forever and the charge step below saw 2 holes instead of 4. Nothing was wrong pre-#553 because confirming a plan wrote all four holes out regardless of who could reach them. Original note follows -- spacing corrected from 4 to 3 (the Drill panel's real default, DEFAULT_SPACING_M): the click drags a 4-unit (8,8)-(12,12) rectangle, and round(4/3)+1 = 2 either way, so the hole COUNT this file originally declared (2x2=4) already happened to match by coincidence -- but the declared spacing value did not match what the click actually uses, so corrected for accuracy per the same principle as the first drill_plan step above, even though no assertion here was actually at risk.

expect.note: #553: ordering only -- the four holes are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, drained by the step below.

steps.description: #553: the driller and the drill_rig cross the pit from the first pattern at (15,15) to this one at (8,8) and sink all four holes. Sandbox-measured pad.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped `cash: 28108` -- a real CI run read 28156, $48 over. Not replaced with increased/decreased: the charge cost itself is flat and mode-invariant, but the cash *entering* this step already carries whatever real-time payroll drift accrued from every click/wait earlier in the file, and that drift's sign isn't consistent run to run -- no single relative claim holds. chargedCount still proves the charge itself landed.

Explicitly switches to the Sequence tab (data-step="3") first -- relying on the panel's own autoAdvance to land there was unverified and, per a real interaction-mode run, wrong here (element present but zero-size, i.e. a hidden inactive tab). Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts) so a click can target it unambiguously. 1 decrement click: 25ms default -> 20 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms).

expect.note: #593-followup (issue #586 CI): `deathCount` is not hard-asserted here -- a genuine command-vs-interaction-mode divergence, same class as the driver-position timing gaps already documented elsewhere in this batch (e.g. level1-playthrough-win.json's own blast step). Command mode's per-tick model has the replacement driller (#5) dismounted and clear of the pattern (traced at (17,13)) by the time this blast fires, so command mode reads deathCount:2; real interaction mode's continuous movement has them still close enough to the (24,24)-(27,27) pattern for the blast to catch them, so a real CI run reads deathCount:3 -- confirmed directly, not assumed. The manager (#3) and the driver (#4) stay clear of it either way. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): `cash` stays dropped too -- inherits the same real-time-accrual drift as the charge step above, and the blast itself is cash-neutral (deaths don't deduct immediately), so there is nothing left to assert about cash at this checkpoint.
